The first release of QwFNfer-xpu, the Intel Arc Pro B70 (SYCL) fork of QwFNfer.

**Downloads**

- `qwfnfer-linux-x86_64-cuda.zip`, `qwfnfer-windows-x86_64-cuda.zip`, `SHA256SUMS`: the NVIDIA CUDA bundles, built as upstream builds them (the fork keeps the CUDA and Windows paths working; CI checks them on every push).
- The B70 engine is built from source: [`docs/BUILDING.md`](https://github.com/ccabrerah/QwFNfer-xpu/blob/v0.5.0/docs/BUILDING.md) (llama.cpp at the pinned commit plus the ggml-sycl patch series in `patches/ggml-sycl/`, then the engine), and [`docs/RUNNING.md`](https://github.com/ccabrerah/QwFNfer-xpu/blob/v0.5.0/docs/RUNNING.md) / `scripts/b70/qwfn-b70.sh` to run it with the adopted switches.

**Changes since v0.4.0** (the tag of 2026-10-14, the last tree with every experimental switch)

- **A slimmer fork.** Every custom behaviour is behind a switch and off by default; the launcher turns the adopted ones on. Features that were built, measured and not worth keeping were removed, each written up with its numbers and the reason in [`docs/dropped-features.md`](https://github.com/ccabrerah/QwFNfer-xpu/blob/v0.5.0/docs/dropped-features.md) (start there before trying an idea again).
- **Rebased onto llama.cpp master a0e6dc7**, and llama.cpp's own work used where it does what our patches did: one-token Q8_0 matvecs on its exact ESIMD kernel, the hyper-connection mixer as `DSV4_HC_PRE`, the decode indexer as `LIGHTNING_INDEXER`, its AVX2 Q2_0 CPU kernel. Upstream QwFNfer's v0.3.0 work merged in (Windows support, CI, release bundles).
- **Decode on the B70, four rounds of bit-identical work** (ggml-sycl patches 37-40, the engine's node order for patch 39): the small glue kernels of a decode or verify step folded into their neighbours; a verify step's q8_0 matvecs of one input as one launch; the expert down projections of a verify step in one launch instead of one per position; the shared expert's SwiGLU inside the merged gate + up launch; a decode indexer kernel that reads each key row once; a cheaper deterministic top-k emit. Measured side by side against the stack of 2026-10-16, as served with the draft head: **decode time -6.8% at short context and -4.7% at 52K context** (layer graphs -8.9% / -7.1%), with the output bit-identical throughout (the decode logits hash, below, unchanged by every round).
- **The vision tower on the GPU** (`--vision-gpu`): ~18x faster image encodes (a 1400x1000 image 31.3 -> 1.7 s), borrowing ~3 GB from the expert tier per encode.
- **A streamed prompt lends only what it needs** (`QWFN_LEND_FIT`), layer by layer, and the refill of the lent layers after a prompt now also runs before the draft head's verify steps (it ran only when a prompt-boundary checkpoint split the prompt).
- **Tried and shelved:** the decode indexer in another summation order (patch 41): 4x faster per call, but ~0 at short context and under 1% at 52K against the bit-identical kernel, and no longer bit-identical. Not enough gain for the code; the details are in `docs/dropped-features.md`.
- **Verification tools in `qwfn-gen`:** `QWFN_HASH_DECODE` (a hash of every replayed position's logits: two runs agree only if every logit does) and `QWFN_LOGITS_SAVE` / `QWFN_LOGITS_CMP` (how far a change that is not bit-identical drifts: top-1 agreement, KL, log-probability changes). Every switch and variable: [`docs/PARAMETERS.md`](https://github.com/ccabrerah/QwFNfer-xpu/blob/v0.5.0/docs/PARAMETERS.md); everything tried, with its measurements: [`docs/B70-registry.md`](https://github.com/ccabrerah/QwFNfer-xpu/blob/v0.5.0/docs/B70-registry.md).
